title: Why the Person at the Door Determines Everything
content:
###  **The Variable Nobody Talks About** 

Most conversations about field marketing focus on territory selection, timing, and messaging. Those things matter. But they are not the biggest variable. 

Put two representatives on the same street, on the same day, with the same information about the same company — and the results will not be close. One will come back with a handful of genuine conversations and scheduled follow-ups. The other will come back having knocked the same number of doors with almost nothing to show for it. 

###  **What Actually Separates Them** 

It is not effort, and it usually is not training. It is temperament. 

Some people are energized by talking to strangers. They read a homeowner's mood in the first three seconds and adjust. They are not thrown by a closed door or a short answer. A day of eighty conversations leaves them in a good mood. 

Other people find the same day exhausting, and homeowners can sense it before a word is spoken. 

###  **Why This Is So Often Overlooked** 

Temperament is hard to screen for and easy to fake in an interview. Availability is easy to verify. So most companies hiring field staff optimize for the thing they can measure, and end up with a team that is present but not effective. 

###  **What We Do About It** 

We hire for the first trait, not the second. It takes longer, costs more, and means passing on a lot of people who would technically do the job. It is also the single reason our field results differ from what most companies experience when they try this themselves.
